slides.texte_overlay:
Social skills that will make you
unforgettable
Learn to include the quiet one. In a group, notice who hasn't spoken yet and bring them in. "Wait, Sam, you lived in Berlin, right?" They'll be grateful all night, and everyone sees you did it.
Learn to give a compliment and move on. "That jacket is great." Then keep talking. No waiting for a reaction, no making it weird. A light compliment with no agenda is the one people actually believe.

Learn to change the subject smoothly. When a chat gets tense or dull, build a bridge. "Speaking of trips, did anyone see that guy who biked across Iceland?" Steering a room without anyone noticing is a real skill.

Always have a good question ready. Five minutes a day of history, art or science gives you real material. "If you could live in any century, which one?" Then actually know something about their answer.
slides.texte_sophia: Always have a good question ready. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. Ask about any century, then actually know something about it.

slides.texte_overlay: Learn to laugh for real. Not the polite "haha" while your mind is somewhere else. When something's funny, let it out. People love being around someone who actually enjoys them, and a real laugh is contagious.
Learn to talk up your friends when they're not there. "You have to meet Tom, he's the funniest guy I know." It always comes back around, and people remember who made them look good.
Learn to leave people better than you found them. End every chat on something warm. "This was fun, good luck with the move." The last thing you say is what they remember on the way home.
